purpose: Three enlarged battlefield layouts, retaining central core and two bottom entrances.

jobs.title: 错位组织岛
jobs.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Create ONE NEW enlarged complete level map for CellDefense, using the supplied map ONLY as a reference for art direction, materials, colors and the protected core. Recompose the battlefield rather than reproducing its layout.
The user wants a genuinely larger PLAYABLE AREA: show a wider battlefield, camera zoomed out approximately 1.5x, about 24 by 18 gameplay-cell proportions instead of the earlier 15 by 11 field. Objects, cells, boundary fibers and the core look SMALLER relative to the entire frame; more usable terrain and more room for tower placement. Landscape 4:3 composition, target 2048x1536, one full-frame coherent map.
Strict 90-degree top-down cartoon PIXEL ART. Crisp stepped pixel outlines, clean flat colors, simple shallow shadows, uniform pixel clusters; no photorealism, blur, dithering, noisy grain or excessive layered relief.
Warm peach/coral tissue ground, warm ivory collagen, dark raspberry wounds. Thin tissue perimeter, about 3% of the frame. Sparse decorative clusters only near the outer rim. Quiet floor with low-contrast broad tissue-cell impressions, plenty of empty usable space.
FIXED GAMEPLAY INVARIANTS:
1. ONE protected core exactly at the center (50%,50%): the recognizable three ivory cells inside a teal membrane, compact, ONLY about 5–6% of the total image width.
2. EXACTLY TWO enemy entry wounds, both on the BOTTOM EDGE, centered near x=15% and x=85%, opening upward into the arena. Bottom-left and bottom-right. No entrance at the top or left/right side edges.
3. Solid obstacles are low peach tissue islands wrapped with cream collagen, clearly distinct from the flat floor. No rock, soil, mechanical wall or grass. Obstacle shapes are simple and readable, with one shallow coral contact shadow. They make enemies take broad gentle bends, not a maze.
4. Keep at least 65% of interior open. All passage gaps stay very wide, at least 10% of image width when practical and never narrower than two core diameters. There are generous build areas beside the approaches. Every entry can reach the core. No sealed ring around the core, dead-end trap or narrow choke point.
5. No towers, tower sockets, enemies, arrows, painted navigation lines, grid, text, labels, buttons, interface or watermark. No collage: only ONE map per output.

MAP VARIANT A — STAGGERED TISSUE ISLANDS / OPEN TWO-APPROACH FIELD.
Place five separate chunky rounded tissue islands at staggered positions:
- lower-left around (28%,72%), medium horizontal oval;
- lower-right around (72%,65%), medium horizontal oval;
- lower-center around (51%,82%), small rounded island, leaving very broad gaps to both lower islands;
- upper-left around (29%,29%), short vertical island;
- upper-right around (72%,25%), small horizontal island.
The lower-left and lower-right islands intercept the direct diagonal approaches from the two entrances. Enemies curve around either side of them and enter a large clear central plaza with the core. Only gentle detours. Offset the left and right approach geometry for a natural asymmetry, without visual clutter. Each island occupies about 11–17% of image width, so the large scale of the field is obvious. Keep a particularly spacious halo of empty ground around the core.

MAP VARIANT C — BROAD SIDE PROMENADES / OPEN CENTRAL COURTYARD.
Build a large central courtyard around the protected core, with three DISCONNECTED gently curved tissue banks outside it:
- a broad low horizontal crescent below the core, centered at (50%,73%), spanning approximately x=36–64%;
- a short vertical curved bank well to the left of the core, centered at (27%,47%);
- a short vertical curved bank well to the right of the core, centered at (74%,42%).
The curves are organic peach tissue lined with ivory fiber, shallow and simple, not giant raised cliffs. The three banks MUST NOT connect or form an enclosing wall. Leave conspicuously wide diagonal gaps between the bottom crescent and each side bank, and an entirely open upper half of the central courtyard.
From each bottom entrance the floor opens into a broad outer apron, then a roomy side passage around the end of the crescent, then back inward to the core. This produces a short readable sweeping detour. Side passages are wide enough for several cells abreast.
Add just one small rounded island in the upper-left open area around (37%,22%) for variation; keep all other upper-floor space empty.
